claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your situation.

First, do you have any children that you're responsible for?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I do. I have a 4-year-old named Alex who lives with me at home. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for them.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! 

To help determine your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask: Do you currently live in the UK?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Great! And just to confirm - are you responsible for Alex's care? For example, do you provide for their needs such as food, clothes, and their general upkeep?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for Alex's care - I provide everything they need like food, clothes, and all their general upkeep.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Just a couple more questions to complete the assessment.

Has Alex ever been in hospital or residential care for an extended period, or are they currently in care or hospital?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Well, Alex was in care for a short while - just about a month or so - but they're back home with me now.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for sharing that information. To understand your situation better, I need to ask a few follow-up questions about Alex's time in care:

How long ago did Alex return home from care?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: They're back home with me now - they returned recently from that time in care.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. To be more specific, approximately how many weeks or months ago did Alex return home? This timing is important for determining your Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see what you're asking. Alex was in care for 4 weeks total, and they've been back home with me since then.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying that. And how long has it been since Alex returned home from that 4-week period in care? For example, has it been a few weeks, a few months, or longer?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It was just those 4 weeks in care recently, and they came home after that. It hasn't been very long since they returned.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for clarifying. And just to understand the full picture - while Alex was in care during those 4 weeks, was the local council paying towards their accommodation or maintenance?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the council wasn't paying for their accommodation or maintenance during that time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you. One more question to clarify: During those 4 weeks when Alex was in care, did they spend any time at home with you? For example, did they come home for at least 24 hours per week, or were they in care for the entire 4 weeks without coming home?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, they were in care for the full time during those 4 weeks - they didn't come home during that period.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Just one final question to complete my assessment:

Do you or your partner (if you have one) have an individual income over £60,000 per year? This doesn't affect whether you can *claim* Child Benefit, but it may affect whether there's a tax charge.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'd rather just know about the eligibility for now - can you tell me if I'm eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Good news! **You are eligible to claim Child Benefit for Alex.**

Here's why:

✓ Alex is 4 years old (under 16)
✓ You live in the UK
✓ Alex lives with you and you're responsible for their care
✓ You provide for Alex's needs (food, clothes, general upkeep)
✓ Although Alex was in care for 4 weeks, this is within the 8-week period during which Child Benefit typically continues, and since the local council wasn't paying for their accommodation or maintenance, this doesn't affect your eligibility

Since Alex is now back home with you, you meet all the standard eligibility requirements for Child Benefit.

If you haven't already claimed, you can apply for Child Benefit through HMRC. If you were already receiving it before Alex went into care, your payments should continue as normal now that they're home.

Is there anything else you'd like to know about Child Benefit?
